name: Tax
tagline: Determining, calculating and reporting withholding tax on supplier invoices and payments.
pickerIntro: Two withholding-tax flows, from invoice receipt to payment and reporting, documented as inputs to a proposed WHT engine.

context.label: Solutions
context.text: Withholding tax runs today on Coupa, SAP and manual working papers. The source proposes a central WHT engine that becomes the single WHT data source into SAP and the return working papers, with its calculation data linked to certificate issuance.

context.label: Automation
context.text: Supplier invoices are captured through Coupa and Kofax OCR today. The proposed engine would automate WHT determination, rate selection, tax base identification and calculation, validate WHT before posting, and route exceptions through an automated workflow.

context.label: AI
context.text: No deployed AI capability is documented. "Finance AI Assistance" is mentioned only as a possible reconciliation and analytics layer, alongside Power BI, that the future-state WHT engine could connect to.

context.label: Cross-Functional Collaboration
context.text: WHT determination spans P2P, TDT (Tax Delivery Team), Direct, Local and Group Tax, CFC / CCFO approvers, Procurement, Controlling, CNB, R2R and the vendors and business users who submit and approve invoices.

processes.title: WHT determination in order to invoice
processes.purpose:
This process takes a supplier invoice from submission through P2P receipt and verification to withholding-tax (WHT) determination, calculation, posting and payment. It is documented as the process input for a proposed WHT engine: the engine is expected to check vendor tax status, service type, market rules, tax locality, any existing WHT code and tax treaty or exemption logic, and then calculate the WHT amount on the correct tax base and rate.

Upstream, the flow starts with vendor registration or vendor master maintenance, followed by P2P invoice receipt and invoice verification. The engine should receive key invoice and vendor data from P2P and the vendor master: supplier name and vendor ID, vendor tax status and country or locality code, PO number, goods receipt and invoice reference, invoice amount and taxable base amount, goods or services description, contract and invoice details, any existing WHT code and historical WHT treatment, market-specific WHT rules, tax base and rates, the location of the business (PE) and of the services performed, and the Certificate of Residence.

The intended outputs are a correct WHT code recommendation, the applicable WHT rate, the tax base for the calculation, the calculated WHT amount, a reason code and audit trail for the WHT decision, an exception report for missing or incorrect data, a posted invoice with the correct WHT treatment, and a data feed for WHT reconciliation, return filing, the payment process and WHT certificate issuance.
processes.cadence: Timing and frequency are not specified in the supplied file. The flow is triggered when a user or vendor submits an invoice into the P2P process; WHT is determined and validated before the invoice is posted, and payment and reporting follow.
processes.purposeSummary: Determine, calculate and post **withholding tax** on supplier invoices, with a **proposed WHT engine** replacing user-selected WHT codes.
processes.cadenceSummary: **Timing and frequency are not specified** in the supplied file.
processes.flowNote: This flow includes a proposed WHT engine: engine determination, calculation and pre-posting validation are future-state recommendations rather than current practice.

stages.title: Submit the invoice
stages.detail:
Invoice submitted by user / vendor
Vendor or user submits invoice into the P2P process

User / Vendor: submits invoice and provides supporting documents
stages.description:
The vendor or business user submits the invoice into the P2P process and provides the supporting documents.

Among the inputs the source lists for WHT determination are the contract and invoice details, any existing WHT code, the goods or services description and, where relevant, the Certificate of Residence and historical WHT treatment.

stages.title: Receive the invoice in P2P
stages.detail:
2) Invoice received by P2P
P2P captures invoice details such as PO number, supplier name, amount, tax / locality code and goods / services description
stages.description: P2P receives the invoice and captures its details: PO number, supplier name, amount, tax or locality code and the goods or services description. Invoice capture runs in Coupa, the invoice processing system.

stages.title: Verify the invoice
stages.detail:
3) Invoice verification
P2P validates invoice against PO, goods receipt, vendor master data and basic invoice requirements
stages.description:
P2P validates the invoice against the purchase order, the goods receipt, vendor master data and basic invoice requirements.

Vendor master data, including the vendor's tax status and country or locality code, comes from the upstream vendor registration and vendor master maintenance process.

stages.title: Determine the WHT treatment
stages.detail:
4) WHT engine determination
The WHT engine checks vendor tax status, service type, market rules, tax locality, existing WHT code and tax treaty or exemption logic where applicable

WHT Engine: performs automated decisioning for WHT determination, rate selection, tax base identification and calculation

Direct Tax / Local Tax / Group Tax, where applicable: provides WHT technical rules, policy position, market-specific interpretation and approval for complex tax treatment
stages.description:
Future state: the proposed WHT engine checks the vendor's tax status, the service type, market rules, tax locality, any existing WHT code and tax treaty or exemption logic where applicable, and recommends the correct WHT code with a reason code and audit trail for the decision.

The engine is designed to draw on the vendor master data source, the invoice processing system (Coupa), a WHT rule table by country, vendor type, service type and tax code, and market-specific WHT rules, tax base and rates. Direct Tax, Local Tax or Group Tax provide the WHT technical rules, policy position and market-specific interpretation, and approve complex tax treatments.

Today there is no engine: WHT code selection sits within P2P invoice processing and relies on the user's knowledge of the correct treatment.
challenges: P2P relies on user knowledge to select correct WHT treatment

stages.title: Calculate the WHT amount
stages.detail:
5) WHT calculation
The WHT engine calculates the applicable WHT amount based on the correct tax base and WHT rate
stages.description:
Future state: the proposed WHT engine identifies the tax base for WHT, selects the applicable WHT rate and calculates the WHT amount, using the invoice amount and taxable base amount received from P2P.

The outputs of this step are the applicable WHT rate, the tax base for the calculation and the calculated WHT amount.

stages.title: Route exceptions to the right owner
stages.displayTitle: Route exceptions to the right owner
stages.detail:
6) Exception handling
If data is missing, inconsistent or not aligned with WHT rules, exception is routed to the right owner, for example, P2P, TDT, local market team or tax reviewer.

TDT / Tax Delivery Team: reviews exceptions, performs gather and analyse, supports reconciliation and validates complex cases where required

CFC / CCFO: reviews and approves where required under governance or payment approval process
stages.description:
If data is missing, inconsistent or not aligned with WHT rules, the exception is routed to the right owner, for example P2P, TDT, the local market team or a tax reviewer. The proposed design produces an exception report for missing or incorrect data and routes exceptions before posting, through an exception dashboard or workflow tool.

TDT reviews the exceptions, gathers and analyses the underlying information and validates complex cases where required. Direct, Local or Group Tax approve complex tax treatments, and CFC / CCFO review and approve where required under governance or the payment approval process.

Today, where the WHT code or rate turns out to be incorrect, a manual adjustment is required.
challenges: Manual adjustment is required where WHT code or rate is incorrect

stages.title: Post the invoice with the correct WHT treatment
stages.displayTitle: Post the invoice with the correct WHT treatment
stages.detail:
7) Invoice posting
Once WHT code and calculation are validated, invoice is posted with the correct WHT treatment

P2P: owns invoice receipt, invoice verification, WHT code selection where embedded in invoice processing, invoice posting, payment and reporting
stages.description:
Once the WHT code and calculation have been validated, P2P posts the invoice in SAP with the correct WHT treatment.

The target design automates WHT validation before posting; today the WHT code and rate may only be checked after the invoice has been posted, which leads to downstream corrections.
challenges: WHT code and rate may only be checked after invoice posting

stages.title: Process payment and report WHT
stages.detail:
8) Payment and reporting
Payment is processed net of WHT where applicable, and WHT data flows into reconciliation, filing, certificate issuance and reporting

Future-state WHT engine should connect with: Vendor master data source; Invoice processing system / Coupa; SAP posting data; WHT rule table by country, vendor type, service type and tax code; Market WHT certificate and filing tracker; Exception dashboard / workflow tool; Reconciliation and analytics layer, for example Power BI or Finance AI Assistance
stages.description:
P2P processes the payment net of WHT where applicable. The WHT data then flows into reconciliation, return filing, certificate issuance and reporting. TDT supports the reconciliation and today spends time reconciling SAP against the manual return working papers.

In the proposed design the engine provides a single data feed for WHT reconciliation, return filing, the payment process and WHT certificate issuance, with certificate issuance logic linked to the calculation data. It would also connect to a market WHT certificate and filing tracker and to a reconciliation and analytics layer such as Power BI or Finance AI Assistance.
challenges: TDT spends time reconciling SAP and return working papers
Incorrect WHT certificate issuance can happen downstream
P2P relies on user knowledge to select correct WHT treatment
WHT code and rate may only be checked after invoice posting
TDT spends time reconciling SAP and return working papers
Manual adjustment is required where WHT code or rate is incorrect
Incorrect WHT certificate issuance can happen downstream
improvements: Documented improvement: Embed the WHT engine before invoice processing - Expected benefit: reduces incorrect WHT code selection.
Documented improvement: Automate WHT validation before posting - Expected benefit: prevents downstream corrections and manual adjustments.
Documented improvement: Create one WHT data source from the engine into SAP and the return working paper - Expected benefit: reduces reconciliation effort.
Documented improvement: Use exception routing before posting - Expected benefit: reduces rework and late corrections.
Documented improvement: Link WHT calculation data to certificate issuance logic - Expected benefit: improves accuracy of WHT certificates.

Proposed: Future-state WHT engine connected to the vendor master data source, the invoice processing system (Coupa), SAP posting data, a WHT rule table by country, vendor type, service type and tax code, the market WHT certificate and filing tracker, an exception dashboard or workflow tool, and a reconciliation and analytics layer such as Power BI or Finance AI Assistance.

processes.title: WHT in spend to payment
processes.purpose:
This process follows a supplier invoice from receipt through validation, tax determination, approval, posting in SAP, payment proposal and payment execution, and then into the WHT deduction, accounting entries, reporting and reconciliation that feed tax return preparation, WHT certificates and compliance reporting. It is documented as the process input for the proposed central WHT engine.

The immediate upstream processes are Procurement, Vendor Master Data, Requisition to Purchase Order, Contract Management and P2P Invoice Receipt and Verification; tax-relevant data should already be available from supplier onboarding, PO creation and invoice processing before payment is executed. The inputs are supplier master data (tax residency, tax ID, vendor type), PO details, contract and service descriptions, supplier invoice data, invoice approval status, cost centre and GL coding, WHT tax code and tax classification, gross invoice amount and payment amount, and tax treaty or exemption documentation where applicable.

The outputs are the approved invoice, the posted accounting document, the correct WHT code and WHT amount, the net payment amount, the payment confirmation, tax posting entries, the WHT audit trail, reconciliation data, WHT return data, WHT certificate issuance data and compliance and reporting outputs.
processes.cadence: Timing and frequency are not specified in the supplied file. The flow is triggered when a supplier invoice is received through Coupa or Kofax OCR; WHT applicability is reviewed before approval and posting, and payment, WHT deduction and reporting follow.
processes.purposeSummary: Carry **tax-relevant supplier and invoice data** through approval, SAP posting and payment so **WHT is deducted, accounted and reported** correctly.
processes.cadenceSummary: **Timing and frequency are not specified** in the supplied file.
processes.flowNote: This flow includes a proposed central WHT engine: engine determination, calculation and pre-posting validation are future-state recommendations rather than current practice.

stages.title: Receive the supplier invoice
stages.detail:
Supplier invoice received via Coupa / Kofax OCR

Procurement: creates supplier and PO information
P2P: invoice processing, matching, posting and payment preparation
stages.description:
The supplier invoice arrives through Coupa or is captured by Kofax OCR and enters P2P invoice processing.

By this point Procurement has created the supplier and PO information, and supplier master data (tax residency, tax ID, vendor type) should already be available from supplier onboarding.

stages.title: Validate and match the invoice
stages.detail: Invoice validation and matching against PO, contract and vendor data
stages.description: P2P validates the invoice and matches it against the purchase order details, the contract and service descriptions, and the vendor master data. The supplier invoice data and cost centre and GL coding are part of the information carried forward from this step.

stages.title: Determine tax and review WHT applicability
stages.displayTitle: Determine tax and review WHT applicability
stages.detail:
Tax determination including WHT applicability review

TDT: WHT rules, exception reviews and compliance oversight
stages.description:
Tax is determined for the invoice, including a review of whether WHT applies. The review uses the WHT tax code and tax classification, the supplier's tax residency and vendor type, and any tax treaty or exemption documentation. TDT owns the WHT rules and reviews exceptions; P2P carries the determination within invoice processing.

Future state: the proposed central WHT engine, supported by a Vendor Tax Repository, would perform this determination automatically, with exceptions handled through an automated workflow and exception management tool.

stages.title: Approve the invoice
stages.detail:
Invoice approval workflow

Business user: approves goods / services received
stages.description: The invoice passes through the approval workflow. The business user confirms that the goods or services have been received, and the resulting invoice approval status becomes an input to posting.

stages.title: Post the invoice in SAP
stages.detail:
Invoice posting into SAP

Controlling: accounting validation and accrual review
stages.description: P2P posts the approved invoice into SAP, creating the posted accounting document with its cost centre and GL coding, WHT tax code and gross invoice amount. Controlling validates the accounting and reviews accruals.

stages.title: Generate the payment proposal
stages.description: As part of payment preparation, P2P generates the payment proposal for the posted invoices, using the gross invoice amount and the payment amount net of any WHT.

stages.title: Execute the payment
stages.description: CNB executes the payment. The supplier is paid the net payment amount and a payment confirmation is produced.

stages.title: Generate WHT deduction and accounting entries
stages.displayTitle: Generate WHT deduction and accounting entries
stages.detail:
WHT deduction and accounting entries generated

R2R: accounting and reconciliation support
stages.description: The WHT deduction and the related accounting entries are generated in SAP, producing the tax posting entries, the correct WHT code and WHT amount, and the WHT audit trail. R2R provides the accounting support and Controlling validates the accounting.

stages.title: Report and reconcile payments
stages.detail:
Payment reporting and reconciliation

Current state: Coupa, Kofax OCR, SAP, Excel working papers, Local tax filings / portals
Future state: Coupa, Central WHT Engine, Vendor Tax Repository, Power BI Dashboard, Automated workflow/exception management
stages.description:
Payments are reported and reconciled, producing the reconciliation data. R2R provides accounting and reconciliation support and TDT provides compliance oversight.

Today this relies on SAP data and Excel working papers; the future state adds a Power BI dashboard on top of the central WHT engine.

stages.title: Feed tax returns, certificates and compliance reporting
stages.displayTitle: Feed tax returns, certificates and compliance reporting
stages.detail:
Data flows into tax return preparation, WHT certificates and compliance reporting

TDT: WHT rules, exception reviews and compliance oversight
stages.description: The WHT data flows into tax return preparation, WHT certificate issuance and compliance reporting, producing the WHT return data, WHT certificate issuance data and compliance and reporting outputs. TDT provides compliance oversight, and filings are made through local tax filings and portals.

improvements: Proposed: Central WHT Engine as the future-state determination and calculation tool alongside Coupa.
Proposed: Vendor Tax Repository holding supplier tax residency, tax ID and vendor type data for the engine.
Proposed: Power BI dashboard for WHT reporting and reconciliation.
Proposed: Automated workflow and exception management in place of manual exception handling.
